description: VERIFIED DEFECT — `schemas/src/versions.ts` lags koine on FOUR of six specs, and omits a sixth entirely. On disk today: kcb 0.2.0 (koine: 0.3.0) · kinp 0.2.0 (koine: 0.2.1) · kgp 0.4.0 (koine: 0.5.0) · kft 0.3.0 (koine: 0.4.0) · kcs 0.2.0 (matches) · **kmi — ABSENT**, though agora ships a KMI runtime (`translation/`, the OTIO engine from chief/30) and koine's KMI is 0.3.0. For a runtime commons whose entire premise is 'koine specifies, agora implements', a silently stale pin table is the most damaging bug class available: every gate that asserts against it goes green while asserting the wrong thing. Note the file's own comment already names the risk — the pins exist in THREE languages (this file, `agora_provider_router.KCB_VERSION` in Python, and the Erlang constant the conformance suite checks) and the only thing keeping the polyglot split honest is a test that compares them to EACH OTHER. Nothing compares any of them to KOINE. That is the actual hole: the gates check internal consistency, not conformance. Scope: (1) repin all four lagging specs and ADD the missing kmi pin, in lockstep across the TypeScript, Python, and Erlang constants — the CLAUDE.md rule is 'bump one, bump all or those gates go red'; (2) decide and record, per spec, whether pinning to a CANDIDATE koine version is correct — four of koine's six specs are candidate, and ingest currently compares majors only, so a producer that moved first is not rejected: state the policy rather than leaving it emergent; (3) add the DRIFT GATE that is missing — a check that reads koine's spec headers and fails when agora's pins disagree, following the ecosystem's vendor-with-drift-gate pattern (a byte-identical mirror plus a test that fails on drift), with a defined behaviour when koine is not checked out beside agora (skip with a loud notice, never silently pass). SUBSUMES `chief/58-kgp-version-pin-advance`, which addresses only the KGP row of the same defect — retire it when this lands. Related: the koine-side half of standards hygiene is `koine:76-upstream-standards-pins` (koine's pins on the OUTSIDE world); this is agora's pins on koine. Also relevant to the MCP surface work in `chief/54`: MCP's 2026-07-28 revision is breaking (stateless — no `initialize`, no session id, per-request `_meta` — plus a mandatory `server/discover`), so agora's MCP surface needs a named target revision, not an implicit one.
verify: node -e "const v=require('fs').readFileSync('schemas/src/versions.ts','utf8'); for (const k of ['kcb','kinp','kgp','kmi','kft','kcs']) if(!v.includes(k+':')) { console.error('missing pin: '+k); process.exit(1);} console.log('all six spec pins present')"

userStories.title: Repin all six specs in lockstep across TypeScript, Python, and Erlang
userStories.description: Bring the pin table to koine's actual spec headers, add the missing KMI pin, and keep the three-language assertion honest. Read each version from koine's spec header, never from memory or from another agora file.
acceptanceCriteria: schemas/src/versions.ts pins each spec to the version in koine's own spec header — kcb, kinp, kgp, kft, kcs — with each value verified by reading `../koine/specs/<spec>.md`'s `**Spec version:**` line rather than copied from any other source.

A `kmi` entry is ADDED, pinned to koine's media-interchange.md header version, with the same doc-comment convention as its siblings and pointing at `koine/specs/media-interchange.md`; agora ships a KMI runtime, so its absence was a real gap and not a scoping choice.

The Python constant(s) (`agora_provider_router.KCB_VERSION` and any sibling in `trainer/`) and the Erlang constant the conformance suite asserts are moved in the SAME commit — CLAUDE.md's 'bump one, bump all or those gates go red' — and `make check-schemas`, `make check-provider-router`, `make check-router-erl`, and `make check-trainer` are all green.

If moving a pin changes any emitted manifest bytes, the byte-for-byte conformance corpus is regenerated by `capture_python_surface.py` in the same change and the regeneration is called out explicitly in the commit body — never left for a later branch to discover.

userStories.title: Decide and record the candidate-version policy
userStories.description: Four of koine's six specs are at CANDIDATE. Pinning a runtime to a candidate is a real decision with a real downside (the shape can still move), and agora currently makes it implicitly, differently, per spec.
acceptanceCriteria: A stated policy lives next to the pins (in versions.ts's doc comment and in the roadmap) covering what agora does when koine's spec is at candidate: pin forward, hold at the last ratified version, or pin forward only when the change is additive — with the reasoning, and applied consistently to all six rows.

The existing behaviour that softens the risk is documented rather than assumed: ingest compares MAJORS only, so a conformant producer that moved first is not rejected — and the policy states where that tolerance does and does not apply.
Any row where agora deliberately does NOT track koine's current version records the reason and the condition that would move it, so a lagging pin is visibly a decision rather than an oversight.
chief/58-kgp-version-pin-advance is retired as subsumed — its KGP row is covered here — and ROADMAP.md's Phase F is updated to point at this tasklist instead.

userStories.title: Add the drift gate that compares agora's pins to koine, not to itself
userStories.description: Today three constants are asserted against EACH OTHER, which catches a partial bump and nothing else. Add the check that catches the failure that actually happened: all three agreeing on a version koine left behind.
acceptanceCriteria: A check in the schemas gate reads the `**Spec version:**` header from each of koine's six spec files and FAILS when any agora pin disagrees, with an error naming the spec, agora's pin, koine's version, and the file to edit.

The check has a defined behaviour when koine is not checked out beside agora (CI, a fresh clone, a container): it SKIPS with a loud, explicit notice — never silently passes, and never hard-fails a build that has no way to satisfy it. Which mode ran is visible in the output.

The gate follows the ecosystem's vendor-with-drift-gate pattern and is wired into `make check-schemas` (and therefore `make check` and `.chief/verify.sh`), so a future koine bump surfaces on the next run rather than at the next audit.
The gate is tested both ways: a passing case with the pins correct, and a failing case with a deliberately wrong pin that produces the expected error — proving it can actually go red.
